request: the payments client that calls the charge service with retries

defects.description: send never compares elapsed time with the deadline: every attempt gets the full per-attempt timeout and the retry loop only stops on the attempt count, so a call with a 1500 ms deadline against an upstream that never answers keeps retrying and backing off for 3300 ms.

trigger.input: server.always('hang'); client.send('GET', '/charges', undefined, { deadlineMs: 1500 }); read clock.now() afterwards (fake clock, sleep advances it)
trigger.expected: the call stops by 1500 ms of clock time and returns { ok: false, error: 'deadline exceeded' } (README: every attempt and every backoff sleep together finish within deadlineMs)

defects.why_missed: The only deadline test asserts ok is false, which is also true when the call overruns its budget; no test reads the clock after a call that times out.
defects.severity_rationale: A hanging upstream returns only after the declared deadline on a supported request, producing a visible timeout and delay.
defects.expected_behavior: the call stops by 1500 ms of clock time and returns { ok: false, error: 'deadline exceeded' } (README: every attempt and every backoff sleep together finish within deadlineMs)
defects.failure_condition: server.always('hang'); client.send('GET', '/charges', undefined, { deadlineMs: 1500 }); read clock.now() afterwards (fake clock, sleep advances it) -> D1 elapsed=3300ms budget=1500ms calls=3 result={"ok":false,"error":"timeout"}

detection_criteria.mechanism: send never compares elapsed time with the deadline: every attempt gets the full per-attempt timeout and the retry loop only stops on the attempt count, so a call with a 1500 ms deadline against an upstream that never answers keeps retrying and backing off for 3300 ms.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the injected fault, the expected degradation, and the observed wrong behaviour.

defects.description: A new idempotency key is generated on every attempt instead of once per logical POST, so when a charge is applied but its response is lost the retry carries a different key, the service cannot recognise it and the customer is charged twice.

trigger.expected: one charge (README: a logical POST carries one idempotency key, the same on every retry, so the service applies it at most once)

defects.why_missed: The retry test uses a 503, which the service never processed, and the key test looks at a single attempt; no test loses a response after the charge was made, the only case where key reuse matters.
defects.severity_rationale: A charge whose successful response is lost can be applied twice when its retry uses a new idempotency key.
defects.expected_behavior: one charge (README: a logical POST carries one idempotency key, the same on every retry, so the service applies it at most once)
defects.failure_condition: server.script(['lost']); client.send('POST', '/charges', { amount: 40 }); server.charges.length -> D2 ok=true calls=2 charges=2

detection_criteria.mechanism: A new idempotency key is generated on every attempt instead of once per logical POST, so when a charge is applied but its response is lost the retry carries a different key, the service cannot recognise it and the customer is charged twice.
detection_criteria.proof: Show the record lost, duplicated or corrupted, and the operation sequence that does it.
